events.title: BD. OF ELECTION COMM'RS, ET AL. V. NAACP, ET AL.
events.summary: The Supreme Court vacated the judgment in the case of BD. OF ELECTION COMM'RS, ET AL. V. NAACP, ET AL. and remanded it to the United States District Court for the Southern District of Mississippi for further consideration in light of the decision in Louisiana v. Callais. Justice Jackson dissented, arguing that the case only presented the question of Section 2’s private enforceability, which was not addressed in Louisiana v. Callais, and thus saw no basis for vacating the lower court’s judgment.
events.why_relevant: The decision affects the enforceability of voting rights under Section 2, impacting democratic processes.

events.title: TURTLE MOUNTAIN BAND, ET AL. V. HOWE, SEC. OF STATE OF ND
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of TURTLE MOUNTAIN BAND, ET AL. V. HOWE, SEC. OF STATE OF ND, vacated the judgment, and remanded the case to the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit for further consideration in light of Louisiana v. Callais. Justice Jackson dissented, stating that the case only involved the question of Section 2’s private enforceability, which was not addressed in Louisiana v. Callais.
events.why_relevant: The decision impacts the interpretation and enforcement of voting rights, which is crucial for fair representation.

events.title: Certiorari Denied for Tony Carruthers v. Tennessee
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States denied the application for a stay of execution and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Tony Carruthers v. Tennessee. The application was initially presented to Justice Kavanaugh, who referred it to the full Court. The denial means that the execution of the death sentence will proceed as scheduled, and the Court will not review the case.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari and stay of execution affects the administration of justice and the finality of capital punishment cases.
